transcript:
>> Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
In the Oval Office Monday, President Trump questioned the release on bail of five British
nationals arrested in the UK near a US-run airbase in England.
>> Might be, but I will tell you, I would have said, don't let them have cashless bail.
I wonder, is it cashless bail, I guess?
That was one of the problems that we had which started the whole mess of crime, and we're
ending cashless bail.
>> The UK's head of counterterrorism policing says the men face stringent conditions and
remain under investigation.
They were detained Sunday near a British military base used by the US to launch strikes on Iran.
Investigators looking into a possible link to Iran, also Russia, or non-state-backed
military groups.
A bill to reform college athletics has cleared its biggest hurdle to date, the Protect College
Sports Act, passed the Senate by a vote of 77 to 22 late Monday night.
Here's NPR's Becky Sullivan.
>> Supporters of the bill say it's needed to curtail chaos in college sports, where
lawsuits have chipped away at longstanding NCAA rules around amateurism, transfers, and
eligibility.
The legislation would give the NCAA a limited antitrust exemption in order to restore some
of those rules.
Critics felt it didn't go far enough to rein in other runaway spending on things like recruiting
and facilities and coaching salaries.
This was a bipartisan bill with bipartisan opposition, yeas and nays came from Republicans
and Democrats alike.
In a statement, NCAA President Charlie Baker thanked senators, but noted there's still
much work left to do.
The bill is supported by President Trump, but first it must pass the House, which has
gone on recess until after the midterms.
Becky Sullivan and PR News.
>> Open AI says it's delaying the release of a new artificial intelligence model out
of security concerns.
Open AI's decision Monday came a day before AI executives started to meet with President
Trump.
Separately, Open AI is apologizing for the hacking of an Australian government website.
The hack in June was made public last week.
August wildfires ravaged whole neighborhoods in Spokane, Washington on Monday.
Governor Bob Ferguson released details on the scope of the damage, Lisa Lineberger
from Spokane Public Radio reports.
Governor Ferguson says that 649 homes were burned by the Spokane complex fires this summer.
He says the losses totaled more than $188 million.
The figures are part of a major disaster declaration Ferguson sent to the president.
>> This is going to take a long time to dig out from this and to get folks the help that
they need.
So we're here from the long haul.
>> The governor's declaration requests additional funds to help both residents and public entities
recover from the fires.
Officials say this is one of Washington's worst fire seasons on record.
In addition to the Spokane complex fires, there have been numerous wildfires in Central
and Eastern Washington.
>> This is NPR News.
Hurricane Polo has made landfall.
The National Hurricane Center in Miami says Polo came ashore of Mexico's Baja California
Peninsula and is expected to remain a hurricane when it makes a second landfall on the Mexican
mainland.
Forecasters are warning of life-threatening winds and flash flooding.
Further west, forecasters say Hurricane Nolo is edging away from the main Hawaiian islands.
A man who spent decades on Utah's death row is being released on bail.
Prosecutors say newly analyzed DNA evidence does not link 71-year-old Douglas Stuart Carter
to a 1985 killing.
A judge ordered the release hours after a bond hearing on Monday.
>> A British chess prodigy has become the youngest player to earn the title "Woman Grandmaster."
And she's only 11 years old, and Piers Lauren Frayer has more from London.
>> Bodhana Sivanandhan uses a booster seat to reach the chessboard.
She's Britain's youngest women's chess champion and the youngest person overall to represent
England internationally in any sport.
On Sunday at the 46th Chess Olympiad in Uzbekistan, she clinched the highest title a female player
can attain, and she'll hold it for life.
She told reporters there...
>> I want to keep going and keep making history as well instead of just stop here.
>> In addition to traveling the world to play chess tournaments, Bodhana is in the British
equivalent of sixth grade and is on her way home now to catch up on school assignments.
Lauren Frayer, NPR News, London.
>> And I'm Giles Snyder.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: President Trump questions UK decision to release five British nationals on bail near US airbase
Protect College Sports Act passes Senate 77-22, giving NCAA limited antitrust exemption
OpenAI delays release of new AI model over security concerns before Trump meeting
OpenAI apologizes for hacking of Australian government website in June
Spokane complex wildfires burned 649 homes, caused $188 million in losses this summer
Hurricane Polo makes landfall on Mexico's Baja California Peninsula, expected to remain hurricane
Hurricane Nolo moves away from main Hawaiian islands
Man released on bail from Utah death row after DNA evidence reanalyzed
British chess prodigy Bodhana Sivanandhan becomes youngest Woman Grandmaster at age 11
